patch.value:
This plan records the current whole-system review under the philosophy project management = context management. Core behavior is unusually well protected: literal all-source coverage, zero local code clones, public SDK boundary enforcement, contract generation, token budgets, security scans, isolated package dogfood, and merge-aware git storage. The most important delivery principle is simplification without capability loss: consolidate presentation grammar, decompose implementation modules and folders, and single-source package policy while retaining every typed SDK primitive, compatibility alias, storage invariant, and history record.

Recommended delivery order:
- Restore the fixed 10k latency and RSS budgets through pm-hcrmye; continue pm-801d and the scale program after the regression is understood.
- Execute the accepted noun-verb grammar and tiered-discovery sequence under pm-n7rr, preserving hidden aliases and contract parity.
- Decompose saturated files through pm-yh8r and reorganize high-fan-out domain folders through pm-kb5h while keeping public SDK exports stable.
- Retain pm-usfg as the functional SDK completeness contract; use pm-f4yn, pm-j8vq, and the quality/security lineages for maintainability and analyzer debt.
- Establish pm-feecbs under the trust ladder, then apply pm-quzx dependency and canonical-package decisions across all official packages.
- Prioritize open mutation races pm-khdq and pm-zwib plus fresh-init/merge-fence issues before claiming conflict-free multi-agent operation at fleet scale.
- Preserve authoritative TOON item documents, append-only attributable history, semantic merge drivers, strict reconciliation, bounded context outputs, and SDK-first implementation in every tranche.

No product source, test, documentation, dependency, workflow, threshold, or release asset is changed by this plan.
Holistic pm CLI, SDK, and ecosystem optimization roadmap

Manual whole-system review and deduplicated delivery map for the pm CLI, public SDK, repository architecture, multi-agent storage semantics, agent UX, performance, security, and official external package fleet.

All current pm items and official packages are evaluated from live state; every finding is mapped to a canonical owner or a duplicate-checked focused item; measured regressions include reproducible evidence and fixed non-weakenable budgets; plan captures sequencing across CLI, SDK, architecture, performance, security, multi-agent safety, and packages; no implementation code or generated changelog is changed; tracker integrity passes; tracker-only commit is pushed directly to main.
A deduplicated, evidence-backed roadmap makes pm simpler, faster, safer, more extensible, and easier for agents without feature loss.
Future agents can resume from live canonical owners instead of repeating broad review work or creating overlapping backlog.
The command surface, SDK, tracker corpus, and official package fleet have all changed materially; current performance and ecosystem-quality evidence must be reconciled before further implementation.
